honest_c3.a_limit_500_wide_ci: limit=500 has ~±2pt 95% CI at score=0.25 (4-choice random baseline). Verdict bands account for this; AT_FLOOR includes [0.20, 0.30].
honest_c3.b_byte_fallback_not_bpe: Original 64K BPE tokenizer is genuinely missing from all sources (HF mirror has only best.pt; disk has only dead symlinks; no backup). Byte-fallback is a faithful subset (the model trained with byte_fallback=True so byte IDs 4-259 ARE in-distribution for the embedding layer), but the BPE merge structure (which compresses multi-char pieces into single tokens) is lost. The model effectively sees text at character level. Conclusion: reduced-but-not-broken signal — the LM head can still produce non-uniform next-byte predictions (which is what the model was trained to do via the byte-fallback path). Random would still be ~0.25; non-floor would still be interpretable as substrate signal.

honest_c3.d_head_a_only: ConsciousDecoderV2 has dual heads (head_a=next-token, head_g=prev-token). Per spec §1.2(iii) we use head_a only for loglik. Pre-registered before eval.
honest_c3.e_block_size_512_not_1024: Checkpoint attn.bias is shape (1,1,512,512) → actual training block_size=512. Eval respects this. Byte-level encoding inflates token counts; some HellaSwag 5-shot prompts likely exceed 512 tokens and are LEFT-truncated to keep continuation intact. Truncation rate logged in run.log.
honest_c3.f_dual_blocker_resolution: Original spec called consciousness_laws.py the blocker. We found a 2nd: missing tokenizer artifact. consciousness_laws.py: FIXED. Tokenizer: WORKAROUND (byte-fallback). Both blockers documented in handoff.
